body:
Found while verifying the #1657 NCA spine splitter against 41 real KEPUBs.

The splitter projects every chapter anchor up to the child of their nearest
common ancestor and cuts there. That handles the ordinary Gutenberg/Calibre
shape (`body > div#book-columns > div#book-inner > chapter divs`) and takes the
library from 301 unreachable chapter identities to 46.

The 46 that remain are ONE shape, and it is worth naming because it is not a
long tail — it is a second structural pattern. Some TOC entries are ANCESTORS of
other TOC entries. Measured on Don Quixote (6), `996-h-7.htm.html`, 11 chapter
anchors:

    pgepubid00010 -> div#book-inner/div                      <- a TOC entry
    pgepubid00011 -> div#book-inner/div#pgepubid00010/h3      <- inside it
    pgepubid00012 -> div#book-inner/div#pgepubid00010/h3
    ... 8 more, all inside div#pgepubid00010

The strict NCA is `div#book-inner`; all 11 anchors project to the single child
`div#pgepubid00010`, so they reduce to one cut point and the document is left
whole. Correct and safe under the current rule, but 10 chapters stay unreachable.

The fix is a descent: when every anchor but one projects onto a child that is
ITSELF one of the anchors, recompute inside that child and split there, with the
outer anchor owning the first piece. The prefix/suffix machinery already
replicates the full ancestor open-tag chain, so it should carry over unchanged.

MEASURED IMPACT of leaving it (chapter-TOC entries only, pageList excluded --
pageList anchors are page numbers pointing into a chapter and must never be
split on):

    collapsed chapter identities   301 -> 46
    books with any unreachable ch   32 -> 11
    Don Quixote (6) and (200)       15 -> 13   (this shape, both copies)
    Moby Dick (196)                118 ->  3
    Crime and Punishment x3          9 ->  2   each

So roughly 13 of the 46 are this exact pattern in Don Quixote alone.

NOT a regression and NOT a blocker for the splitter landing: an unsplittable
document degrades to exactly today's behaviour (no split, no rewrite, file
untouched), never to a corrupt package.

resolution.note: Fixed in #1773. Bounded two-stage refinement: the NCA partition runs first, then any resulting piece still owning >=2 chapter-TOC targets gets exactly one refinement pass. Also covers a sub-shape this finding did not name -- an outer anchor plus exactly ONE inner anchor, which a two-inner-cut-point predicate excluded. Measured on the 41-book library: 1584 -> 1610 of 1653 anchorable, no book regressed, all 41 source KEPUBs SHA-256 unchanged. Residue then read at the source: 35 licence footers, 5 title pages, 1 Contents, 1 part divider whose chapter is reachable anyway, and exactly ONE real chapter (Pride and Prejudice, CHAPTER LXI).

title: Spine splitter cannot separate chapters whose TOC anchors nest inside one another
